novel_features.name: One-shot lane bundle
novel_features.description: Get a part's RoHS and REACH verdicts plus the applicable signed TI compliance statement PDFs in one JSON envelope.
novel_features.rationale: Shaped exactly for the cowork extraction lane's manifest mapping — verdicts and evidence artifacts land together, no second call.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when a supplier-extraction run needs verdicts AND evidence documents in a single deterministic call.

novel_features.name: Cookie-freshness probe
novel_features.description: Find out whether the deposited myTI cookie snapshot still works before running a batch of gated extractions.
novel_features.rationale: Distinguishes 'cookies went stale' from 'part not found' — the two failure modes look identical mid-extraction otherwise.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Run it before any part ratings or part fmd batch; a stale result means trigger a fresh HIL login instead of burning lookups.

novel_features.name: Full evidence ladder
novel_features.description: One command that always returns anonymous verdicts and blanket PDFs, and adds the rich ratings table and Class-D FMD XML when cookies work.
novel_features.rationale: Degrades honestly: each rung reports its own status, so the caller sees exactly which evidence tier was available.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when you want the most complete evidence available right now without pre-deciding whether login works.

narrative.headline: TI part compliance without the portal: anonymous RoHS/REACH per orderable, plus cookie-injected FMD Class-D XML and per-part exemptions.
narrative.value_prop: Reads the compliance facts straight off TI's server-rendered product pages with plain HTTP — no login, no browser. When a myTI cookie snapshot is deposited (via the existing Browserbase human-in-the-loop login), the same CLI unlocks the Environmental Ratings table, per-part RoHS exemptions, and IPC-1752A Class-D FMD XML. It never logs in itself and fails closed when cookies are stale.
narrative.auth_narrative: Anonymous commands (part compliance, part coc) need no credentials. Login-gated commands (part ratings, part fmd) consume a cookie snapshot captured by a human login in a Browserbase session — pass it via --cookies <file>. The CLI never performs a login and never sees your password; when cookies are stale it exits with a distinct 'login required' error so the orchestrator can trigger a fresh HIL login.

quickstart.comment: Health check — works without any credentials
Anonymous RoHS/REACH for one orderable part number
Download TI's signed blanket compliance statement PDFs
Verify a deposited myTI cookie snapshot before gated lookups
Fetch the IPC-1752A Class-D FMD XML (requires working cookies)

troubleshoots.symptom: part ratings / part fmd exits with 'login required or cookies stale'
troubleshoots.fix: Trigger a fresh human login via the Browserbase HIL flow and re-deposit the cookie snapshot; myTI invalidates sessions server-side every few hours.

troubleshoots.symptom: part compliance says the orderable was not found on the product page
troubleshoots.fix: Check the OPN spelling; the CLI resolves the generic (TUSB320RWBR → TUSB320) and matches your OPN against the page's orderables list.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when an agent needs Texas Instruments part compliance facts: RoHS/REACH status for an orderable part number, TI's signed compliance statement PDFs as evidence, or (with a deposited myTI cookie snapshot) per-part RoHS exemptions, the SVHC sentence, and IPC-1752A Class-D FMD XML. It is the extraction engine behind the cowork agent's lane:cli route for ti.com.
anti_triggers: Do not use for TI datasheets, pricing, inventory, or parametric search — TI's official product API and web store cover those.
Do not use to log in to myTI — login is always a human-in-the-loop Browserbase flow; this CLI only consumes deposited cookies.
Do not use for non-TI parts; for McMaster-Carr parts use mcmaster-pp-cli.
